# Head of Operations

[Senegal](https://startup.jobs/locations/senegal)

[On-site](https://startup.jobs/)

## TLDR

Oversee agent operations, liquidity, cash security, quality, and training while strengthening the agent network.

## Our mission

We're making Africa the first cashless continent.

In 2017, over half the population in Sub-Saharan Africa had no bank account. That's for good reason—the fees are too high, the closest branch can be miles away, and nobody takes cards. Without access to financial institutions, people are forced to keep their savings under the mattress. Small business owners rely on lenders who charge extortionate rates. Parents spend hours waiting in line to pay school fees in cash.

We're solving this by building financial services that just work: no account fees, instantly available, and accepted everywhere. In places where electricity, water and roads don't always work, you can still send money with Wave. In 2017, we launched a mobile app in Senegal for cash deposit, withdrawal, and peer-to-peer and business payments. Now, we have millions of users across 9 countries and are growing fast.

Our goal is to make Africa the first cashless continent and that's where you come in...

## **How you'll help us achieve it**

We’re looking for a Head of Operations to drive operational excellence across Wave Senegal. You’ll lead key functions spanning agent operations, liquidity, cash security, agent quality, and training, while identifying innovative ways to strengthen our agent network and improve how we operate. You will be in charge of maintaining a high-quality, reliable network, improving operational efficiency, and optimizing costs while ensuring our operations remain efficient, reliable, and customer-focused.

In this role, you'll;

* Oversee daily business operations in Senegal, working from first principles to understand the problems blocking the business' growth and taking ownership of resolving those problems.
* Work closely with Wave's Executive Team to determine key objectives and operationalize strategies.
* Provide direct management of key functional managers within the business.
* Own key projects for Wave Senegal, including developing the strategy and executing what is needed to achieve them.
* Lead by living Wave's values and ensuring they're deeply ingrained within the team.
* Be an advocate for your team within the company more broadly.
* Work with our People Team to identify and hire local talent.
* Help to develop Wave's global strategy by sharing insights and learnings from Senegal.

## **Key details**

* Location: Senegal
* Work authorization in Senegal is required.
* This is a permanent position.
* Our salaries are competitive and calculated using a transparent formula.
* We offer generous health insurance for yourself and your dependents.
* We support working parents - we offer generous parental leave policies (26 weeks for mothers and 4 weeks for fathers) and subsidized childcare when you return to work.
* We help you live your fullest life now! We subsidize gym memberships and fitness classes.
* Airtime reimbursement.
* Free food and a beautiful office space.

## **Requirements**

* Have 10+ years of experience either in mobile money, finance, fintech, telecoms, or technology sectors as a senior leader or executive managing cross-functional teams.
* Hold a bachelor's degree or higher in business administration.
* Have 8+ years of experience building and leading strong teams in achieving results.
* Possess a track record in managing stakeholders through strategic reporting for external partners.
* Strong track record in building country-level and multi-country partnerships in Africa.
* Work authorization in Senegal.
* Fluency in English and, ideally, in a local language.

## **You might be a good fit if you**

* Demonstrate very strong communication and stakeholder management skills, communicating effectively and often, both in writing and in person, to the point of over-communication.
* Can adjust quickly to changing priorities and conditions and cope effectively with complexity and change.
* Are deeply passionate about our mission of bringing financial services to the people who need them the most.
* Are intellectually curious, creative in the way you go about tackling problems, and embrace failure as a means to spark innovation and growth.
* Possess a bias toward action and testing and are analytical in your approach.
* Demonstrate tenacity and a willingness to go the distance to get something done.
* Enjoy owning projects - you're autonomous yet know when to escalate problems.

## Our team

* We have a rapidly growing in-country team in Senegal, Côte d'Ivoire, Mali, Burkina Faso, The Gambia, Uganda, Niger, Sierra Leone, and Cameroon plus remote team members spread across the world.
* We're deeply passionate about our mission of bringing radically affordable financial services to the people who need them most.
* We foster autonomy for our employees. You'll own your projects at every stage, from understanding the problem to monitoring your solution in production.
* We raised the largest Series A in Africa in 2021. Our world-class investors, include Founders Fund, Sequoia Heritage, Stripe, Ribbit Capital, Y Combinator, and Partech Africa.
* We are on [Y Combinator's top companies by revenue](https://www.ycombinator.com/topcompanies/revenue) .

## How to apply

Fill out the form below, and upload a resume in English and a cover letter describing your interest in Wave and the role.

We review applications frequently and recommend that you apply to the role that most closely aligns with your skills, experience and career goals.

Wave is an equal-opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

Free Meals & Snacks

Free food and a beautiful office space.

Health Insurance

Generous health insurance for you and your dependents.

Airtime reimbursement

Paid Parental Leave

Parental leave: 26 weeks for mothers and 4 weeks for fathers.

Wellness Stipend

Subsidize gym memberships and fitness classes.

Clorox is the place that’s committed to growth – for our people and our brands. Guided by our purpose and values, and with people at the center of everything we do, we believe every one of us can make a positive impact on consumers, communities, and teammates. Join our team. [\#CloroxIsThePlace](https://www.linkedin.com/feed/hashtag/?keywords=cloroxistheplace&highlightedUpdateUrns=urn%3Ali%3Aactivity%3A7079847624048001024)

**Your role at Clorox:**

The Production Services team is part of the Food/Burt’s Technical Services organization and is committed to delivering cost savings, quality improvements, supply assurance, qualification, brand maintenance, and technical issue-resolution projects with excellence. You will report to the Technical Services Leader with most of your direct reports being located in Alpharetta GA and Durham NC.

**In this role, you will:**

This position will manage the Food & Burt’s Production Services team to deliver excellent technical support in execution of key PSO and business-critical projects across the Food & Burt’s businesses, including cost savings, supply assurance, brand maintenance, qualifications, quality improvement and innovation support. Ensures effective interfaces between our Production Services organization and PSO, R&D, Quality, Engineering, Procurement, Manufacturing and External Manufacturers. Develops technical and leadership excellence across the team and is recognized as a key business partner and leader by the Product Supply Organization and our functional stakeholders.

  
This role sets multi-year technical capability strategy for Food & Burt’s, leads Production Services standard work across both BUs, and represents the BU in enterprise forums such as the Production Services Community of Practice.

The Food & Burt’s Production Services team serves as business leaders and technical experts across products, packaging, processes, manufacturing systems, external manufacturers, specifications, enterprise wide systems and qualifications. While we sit within the center Business Unit (BU), we are strong partners with our manufacturing plants, EMs, R&D, Quality, Engineering and Procurement teams to ensure great products produced at the best value and continued supply. This work is achieved through activities such as Packaging Material Design/Specs, process/formulation troubleshooting, support of new Innovation development/implementation, data analysis, specification development, laboratory testing, manufacturing line trials, process & equipment support, and cross-functional technical problem solving.

**What we look for:**

_**People & Talent Leadership:**_

  
* Owns Succession Planning and bench strength for Production Services key roles, in line with the BU People Plan; develops Ready-Now successors and builds future-ready technical capability.

* Lead a team of technical professionals supporting Food & Burt’s Production Services across process, packaging and manufacturing.
* Lead a team of up to 6 direct/indirect reports with multi-functional responsibility across the Food & Burt’s BU.  Typical number of direct reports varies from 4-6.
* The majority of the staff is geographically located in Alpharetta, GA or Durham, NC. Direct reports span a grade range level from 23-26.
* Development of PS staff both as technical experts and PSO leaders.
* Leads PSO staff discussions to enable career development of current team and broader PSO individuals.

  
_**Functional & Strategic Leadership:**_

* Member of the Food/Burt’s Technical Leadership Team, evaluating personnel moves, organizational design, capability gaps, technical needs, and resource requirements across the BU.
* Actively interacts with key partners and stakeholders including Director of Manufacturing, Engineering, GSS, Quality, Manufacturing, R&D, Operations, and external manufacturers.
* Ensures proper project prioritization and adequate resource allocation, ensuring the team’s support across multiple business units, sites, external manufacturers, and projects meets business requirements and our customers’ expectations.
* Recognized expert in technical and operational processes required to support the 2 Businesses, including packaging, process equipment, enterprise systems (i.e. SAP S/4, PLM, Engunity, Intelex), qualifications, quality systems, and technical troubleshooting.
* Demonstrates leadership and technical expertise of Production Services WOW
* Ensures delivery of key cost savings, supply assurance, brand maintenance, quality, plant, external manufacturing, and technical issue-resolution initiatives in concert with the business direction.

· Ensure spending controls are in place to meet T&E budget.

_**Portfolio Oversight:**_

* Owns the Food & Burt’s Production Services portfolio, personally leading complex, business-critical or high-risk initiatives.
* Influences Food & Burt’s operating and functional leadership teams to make required decisions, align priorities, provide direction on projects, define scope, and ensure understanding of risks.
* Lead Food and Burt’s Production Services activities across packaging and process workstreams, including planning, qualification, implementation, start-up support, and post-launch stabilization for technical deliverables.
* Serve as the technical resource for packaging materials and process interfaces, supporting materials, equipment readiness, manufacturing capability, external manufacturer alignment, plant trials, line trials, and process validation needs.
* Direct large, complex, multi-site and multi-BU technical programs, setting priorities, action plans, trial plans, decision gates, risk mitigation strategies, and structured problem-solving standards for the team across packaging and process-related issues.
* Develop and maintain specifications, manufacturing readiness documentation, change-management records, technical knowledge, and cross-functional communication to protect supply continuity, quality, cost, compliance, food safety, and manufacturing stability.

**Workplace type:**

This role will require the talent to be located in Alpharetta, GA or Durham, NC and be in office 3x per week in accordance with the Hybrid 2.0 Policy.  
  
  
\#LI-Hybrid  
**Our values-based culture connects to our purpose and empowers people to be their best, professionally and personally. We serve a diverse consumer base which is why we believe teams that reflect our consumers bring fresh perspectives, drive innovation, and help us stay attuned to the world around us. That’s why we foster an inclusive culture where every person can feel respected, valued, and fully able to participate, and ultimately able to thrive.** [**Learn more**](https://www.thecloroxcompany.com/responsibility/thriving-communities/empowering-our-employees-to-thrive/) **.**

  
**[U.S.]Additional Information:**

At Clorox, we champion people to be well and thrive, starting with our own people. To help make this possible, we offer comprehensive, competitive benefits that prioritize all aspects of wellbeing and provide flexibility for our teammates’ unique needs. This includes robust health plans, a market-leading 401(k) program with a company match, flexible time off benefits (including half-day summer Fridays depending on location), inclusive fertility/adoption benefits, and more.

  
We are committed to fair and equitable pay and are transparent with current and future teammates about our full salary ranges. We use broad salary ranges that reflect the competitive market for similar jobs, provide sufficient opportunity for growth as you gain experience and expand responsibilities, while also allowing for differentiation based on performance. Based on the breadth of our ranges, most new hires will start at Clorox in the first half of the applicable range. Your starting pay will depend on job-related factors, including relevant skills, knowledge, experience and location. The applicable salary range for every role in the U.S. is based on your work location and is aligned to one of three zones according to the cost of labor in your area.

  
–Zone A: $131,200 - $258,500

–Zone B: $120,300 - $237,000

–Zone C: $109,400 - $215,500

  
All ranges are subject to change in the future. Your recruiter can share more about the specific salary range for your location during the hiring process.

  
This job is also eligible for participation in Clorox’s incentive plans, subject to the terms of the applicable plan documents and policies.

Please apply directly to our job postings and do not submit your resume to any person via text message. Clorox does not conduct text-based interviews and encourages you to be cautious of anyone posing as a Clorox recruiter via unsolicited texts during these uncertain times.

# Director, Manufacturing Engineering

Lewisville, TX, United States

## Job Description

Reports to: Senior Vice President, Operations, and Transformation

Scope: 8 U.S. Manufacturing Facilities

The Director of Manufacturing Engineering provides enterprise leadership for manufacturing process excellence, automation, and asset reliability across Overhead Door Corporation’s U.S. manufacturing footprint. This role is responsible for developing and executing a unified manufacturing engineering and maintenance strategy that enables world-class productivity, equipment uptime, and technological advancement. The leader will integrate engineering, maintenance, and facilities functions under a single vision — driving automation, digitalization, and Total Productive Maintenance (TPM) within the OHD Lean Operating System. This position blends strategic system design with hands-on execution, ensuring that process capability, reliability, and cost effectiveness improve year over year across all sites.

## Responsibilities

Manufacturing Engineering Leadership

* Lead the enterprise Manufacturing Engineering strategy to improve process capability, throughput, and cost efficiency.
* Define and deploy standard manufacturing methods, best practices, and process documentation across all plants.
* Partner with Operations and Product Engineering to ensure manufacturability and scalability of new products.
* Oversee major capital investments, layout optimization, and capacity planning initiatives.

Automation, Digitalization & Smart Factory

* Develop and implement the corporate automation roadmap to drive productivity, consistency, and labor efficiency.
* Lead digital transformation through implementation of smart manufacturing systems, MES, and IoT technologies.
* Integrate equipment monitoring, predictive analytics, and real-time performance dashboards.
* Evaluate and deploy robotics, vision systems, and advanced automation to improve safety and reduce waste.

Maintenance & Total Productive Maintenance (TPM)

* Own enterprise maintenance and reliability strategy, driving TPM deployment and asset lifecycle management.
* Establish preventive and predictive maintenance programs focused on reducing unplanned downtime and maintenance cost.
* Standardize maintenance planning, CMMS utilization, and spare parts management across plants.
* Drive MTBF (Mean Time Between Failures) and MTTR (Mean Time to Repair) improvements year-over-year.

Facilities & Capital Planning

* Oversee facilities management, including infrastructure maintenance, utilities, and energy optimization.
* Ensure all facility projects meet regulatory, environmental, and safety standards.
* Lead annual capital planning process and long-term asset renewal strategy.
* Drive energy efficiency and sustainability improvements in partnership with EHS & Sustainability leadership.

Technical Capability & Continuous Improvement

* Build an enterprise-level technical capability roadmap for engineers, technicians, and maintenance professionals.
* Lead advanced problem-solving using Six Sigma, root cause analysis, and reliability-centered maintenance techniques.
* Integrate engineering and maintenance metrics into site performance dashboards and executive reviews.
* Partner with Lean and Quality to ensure process discipline and adherence to standard work.

Leadership Expectations

* Operates as a strategic transformation leader driving technology and reliability improvements across all sites.
* Fosters a culture of technical excellence, ownership, and continuous improvement among engineering and maintenance teams.
* Balances strategic capital planning with hands-on operational problem solving.
* Influences through data, collaboration, and disciplined execution — not escalation.
* Serves as the corporate champion for automation, TPM, and digital manufacturing innovation.

## Qualifications

* Bachelor’s degree in mechanical, Industrial, Electrical, or Manufacturing Engineering (master’s preferred).
* 10+ years of progressive experience in manufacturing engineering, maintenance, or operations leadership.
* Demonstrated success implementing automation and TPM in multi-site manufacturing environments.
* Proven ability to lead cross-functional technical teams through large-scale transformation initiatives.
* Deep knowledge of Lean Manufacturing, reliability engineering, and digital factory technologies (MES, IoT, robotics).
* Strong leadership, communication, and project management skills.
* Experience in building products, industrial equipment, or discrete manufacturing preferred.
* Willingness to travel up to 50% across U.S. manufacturing sites.
* Position Impact
* This role is foundational in shaping the future of manufacturing for Overhead Door Corporation — combining engineering excellence, automation, and reliability into a single cohesive system. Success will be measured by improved equipment performance, reduced downtime, capital efficiency, and the advancement of digital manufacturing maturity across all plants.

**About Rivian**  
  
Rivian is on a mission to keep the world adventurous forever. This goes for the emissions-free Electric Adventure Vehicles we build, and the curious, courageous souls we seek to attract.

As a company, we constantly challenge what’s possible, never simply accepting what has always been done. We reframe old problems, seek new solutions and operate comfortably in areas that are unknown. Our backgrounds are diverse, but our team shares a love of the outdoors and a desire to protect it for future generations.

  
**Role Summary**  
  
The Director of Supplier Development, Industrialization & Quality will lead a team responsible for end-to-end supplier execution, capability building, tooling industrialization and quality assurance across Rivian's global supply base. Merging pre-PPAP development engineering with post-PPAP quality management, this role establishes a single point of accountability for parts and systems from concept and tooling kickoff through ramp-up and serial production.

The ideal leader brings deep automotive or EV industrialization experience, combining technical rigor with a "boots on the ground" problem-solving methodology to ensure flawless program execution, capacity realization and zero-defect quality across launch and current production vehicles.

  
**Responsibilities**  
  
* **Strategic Organization Leadership:** Build, lead and mentor a high-performing global team of Supplier Development, Industrialization & Quality Engineers across major commodity sectors (e.g. Chassis, Battery, Drive Unit, Thermal, Interior, Exterior and Power Distribution).
* **Cradle-to-Grave Part & Supplier Ownership:** Oversee end-to-end component ownership, streamlining supplier communications and cross-functional alignment across both pre-PPAP development and post-PPAP production quality.
* **Upstream Quality Prevention:** Engage early in program development cycles alongside Engineering and Purchasing to conduct DFM, DFMEA and PFMEA reviews, resolving downstream ramp and quality constraints long before Start of Production (SOP).
* **Tooling & Capacity Industrialization:** Oversee supplier industrialization timelines, tool kickoffs, tooling audits and station-by-station capacity mapping (JPH / throughput modeling, sensor checks and Poka-Yoke validations) to resolve yield bottlenecks and secure confirmed production volumes.
* **Rigorous PPAP & Launch Gatekeeping:** Enforce strict APQP/PPAP gatekeeper discipline, executing Safe Launch containment protocols, Rate-at-Rate verifications and mandatory recovery glide paths for supplier milestones.
* **Rapid Problem Solving & On-Site Triage:** Deploy resources directly to supplier facilities during critical ramps to perform root-cause analyses (5-Why, 8D, PFMEA updates) and drive immediate yield and quality recovery.
* **Supplier Performance & Governance:** Establish and track global supplier scorecards, quality metrics, and audit schedules, driving corrective action plans and ongoing continuous improvement initiatives across the supply chain.
* **Cross-Functional Executive Partnership:** Collaborate closely with Procurement, Hardware Engineering, Manufacturing Operations and Program Management to escalate risks, present recovery models and align sourcing strategies.

  
**Qualifications**  
  
* **Education:** Bachelor’s degree in Engineering (Mechanical, Electrical, Industrial, or Manufacturing), Supply Chain Management or a related technical field. Master’s degree preferred.
* **Experience:** 15+ years of progressive leadership experience in supplier development, supplier quality or manufacturing industrialization within the automotive or high-growth EV sector.
* **Cradle-to-Grave Domain Expertise:** Proven track record of managing components through the entire lifecycle - from early engineering design reviews, APQP and PPAP approval to serial production quality management.
* **Technical Mastery:** Deep proficiency in core quality and manufacturing tools such as APQP, PPAP, PFMEA, SPC, 8D, 5-Why, Poke-Yoke systems and Lean Manufacturing.
* **Operational & Analytical Discipline:** Demonstrated experience in hands-on bottleneck resolution, capacity modeling, line-walk audits and data-driven root-cause problem solving.
* **Leadership & Change Management:** Experience building, restructuring or scaling global technical teams, instilling operational discipline and metric accountability while maintaining startup agility.
* **Communication & Negotiation:** Exceptional interpersonal and executive presentation skills; capable of holding supplier C-suite leadership accountable to Rivian performance expectations.
* **Willingness to Travel:** Ability to travel up to 50% (domestic and international) to engage suppliers directly on-site.

  
**Pay Disclosure**  
  
The salary range for this role is USD $183,000.00-$262,000.00 for Normal, IL and Plymouth, MI based applicants and $201,000-$287,000 for Irvine, CA. This is the lowest to highest salary we in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. An employee’s position within the salary range will be based on several factors including, but not limited to, specific competencies, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, geographic location, shift, and organizational needs.  
  
The successful candidate may be eligible for annual performance bonus and equity awards.  
  
We offer a comprehensive package of benefits for full-time and part-time employees, their spouse or domestic partner, and children up to age 26, including but not limited to paid vacation, paid sick leave, and a competitive portfolio of insurance benefits including life, medical, dental, vision, short-term disability insurance, and long-term disability insurance to eligible employees. You may also have the opportunity to participate in Rivian’s 401(k) Plan and Employee Stock Purchase Program if you meet certain eligibility requirements. Full-time employee coverage is effective on their first day of employment. Part-time employee coverage is effective the first of the month following 90 days of employment. More information about benefits is available at [rivianbenefits.com](http://rivianbenefits.com/) .  
  
You can apply for this role through [careers.rivian.com](https://careers.rivian.com/) (or through [internal-careers-rivian.icims.com](http://internal-careers-rivian.icims.com/) if you are a current employee). This job is not expected to be closed any sooner than 06/27/2026

WHO WE ARE

Rock Manufacturing is a small-caliber ammunition manufacturer based in Sweet Springs, Missouri, producing projectiles, load ammunition, and components, along with in-house loading and priming. Founded in its current form in 2023, we are a well-capitalized company in a high-growth chapter, vertically integrating our production and building toward a significant revenue milestone over the coming year. Our equipment is owned outright and our capital position is strong, which gives us a rare combination of startup speed and financial stability.

Our vision is to deliver the complete spectrum of small-caliber ammunition solutions — projectiles, cases, components, materials, and services — that empower our customers with unmatched reliability.  
  
 Our mission is to support the ammunition industry with top-tier projectiles, cases, components, services, and materials — from copper strip to propellants — delivered with speed, consistency, and integrity. Driven by passion and collaboration, we continuously improve to exceed expectations and ensure reliable performance in every product we make.

Our Core Values are:

* Precision First: We never compromise on accuracy — from material sourcing to final delivery.
* Integrity Always: We do what we say, and we stand behind every round, component, and commitment.
* Customer-Centered: Our partners rely on us. We deliver with responsiveness, reliability, and value.
* Continuous Improvement: We seek better processes, smarter solutions, and higher standards — every day.
* Pride in Production: We take ownership of our work, our machines, and our results.
* American Ingenuity, Global Perspective: We build with American excellence while sourcing and selling with global agility.

We are looking for someone who genuinely connects with our mission and the way we operate, because that alignment is what makes this role succeed.

JOB DESCRIPTION

The Rock Manufacturing team is looking for a results-driven and execution-focused VP of Operations to take full ownership of how the business runs day to day. This is a hands-on integrator role for an operator who turns vision into reality, drives accountability across the floor, and keeps major initiatives moving from idea to completed deliverable.

The VP of Operations is responsible for optimizing the company's day-to-day execution, designing and implementing the infrastructure and processes that boost productivity and efficiency, and freeing the executive team to focus on their highest-value work. The application code word is EMPOWER. The VP of Operations is a driver. They take a high-level goal, figure out the details independently, and hold the team accountable to getting it done.

This role will lead Rock Manufacturing through a chapter of rapid growth and vertical integration. You will be the operational engine who brings follow-through, structure, and momentum to a fast-moving, founder-led manufacturer, working in close collaboration with the leadership team.

This is a boots-on-the-ground, on-site role based at our plant in Sweet Springs, Missouri. Building trust with the production floor is central to your success, so your presence on-site is essential. This is a critical position within the business, and as such, we host a rigorous, 4-part application process.

WHAT MAKES THIS ROLE UNIQUE

You will step into a business that already knows where it wants to go and has built much of what it needs to get there. What it needs now is the person who drives it home. Leadership generates strong ideas and sets clear direction in its weekly leadership meetings, and your job is to convert that direction into executed results, every week, without the momentum stalling.

Your success will ultimately be measured by one outcome: enabling both owners to step fully out of day-to-day operations by the end of the year, with the business running as a self-managing machine. You will take ownership of the operational back end the owners currently carry, including administrative tasks, material sourcing, and quality oversight, so they can focus on growth and technology.

RESPONSIBILITIES (TASKS ASSOCIATED WITH THE ROLE):

Operational Ownership & Execution

* Take ownership of the day-to-day operational back end currently held by leadership, including administrative tasks, material sourcing, and quality oversight
* Convert the deliverables and decisions made in weekly leadership meetings into completed, on-time results
* Drive follow-through and accountability so projects move from discussion to done

Team Leadership & Accountability

* Lead, manage, and develop the production team, building trust and momentum on the floor
* Hold team members accountable to production targets and clear performance standards
* Recruit, train, and promote talent as the team scales across multiple shifts

Systems & Process Implementation

* Design and implement the SOPs, workflows, and systems the business needs to scale
* Build the data and reporting infrastructure that gives leadership clear visibility into production and performance
* Evolve communication and meeting rhythms so the team stays aligned and efficient

Production, Quality & Scaling

* Drive production lines toward full multi-shift capacity, specifically two projectile shifts and one loading shift operational by the end of the year.
* Lead the launch of a major new production operation to fulfill incoming demand
* Improve quality and reduce material scrap, and support bringing key material inputs in-house to strengthen unit economics

Founder Extraction & Communication

* Operate with a high degree of independence, owning the details so leadership does not have to
* Communicate clearly and directly, and provide leadership with concise visual status reports
* Remove operational stress from the executive team as much as possible

REQUIREMENTS (EXPECTED PROFICIENCIES):

Experience Requirements (Non-Negotiable)

* Proven track record scaling a business through the $3M to $20M growth phase, ideally in a manufacturing, production, or operations-heavy environment
* Exceptional project management ability, with a history of driving processes, pushing initiatives forward, and holding teams accountable to deliverables
* A genuine boots-on-the-ground operator who leads from the floor and is energized by being on-site and close to the work
* Direct experience in ammunition manufacturing is helpful but not required. What matters is operational excellence and the ability to learn a production environment quickly

Core Competencies

* Strong systems and process thinking, with the ability to design and roll out SOPs that the team actually uses
* Data and KPI proficiency to establish, track, and act on the metrics that drive production performance
* Change management skill to bring structure and consistency to a fast-moving team
* An execution-first orientation, comfortable operating in the details and getting hands-on to make targets happen

Critical Soft Skills (Deal-Breakers)

* Exceptionally clear, candid, and direct communicator
* Comfortable with blunt, fast-paced feedback, able to keep it strictly business and move forward quickly
* A natural accountability owner who is willing to have the direct conversations that keep standards high
* Decisive and self-directed, able to take a high-level vision and independently figure out the path to execution

Technical & Logistical Requirements

* Able to work on-site full time in Sweet Springs, Missouri (relocation support available for the right candidate.
* Exceptional attention to detail, time-management, and organizational skills
* Data-driven decision maker who can analyze information and act on it
* Highly resourceful self-starter who thrives without direct supervision
* Experienced with ERP implementation in a manufacturing environment

Mindset & Cultural Fit

* You hold yourself to the highest standards of performance and stay resilient in the face of obstacles
* You thrive in a fast-changing, high-ownership environment and are energized by doing what it takes to hit production targets during a critical build phase
* You take ownership rather than make excuses, and you treat every challenge as something to solve
* You are comfortable with autonomy and motivated by the chance to build something and see it through

* First 30 days: Immerse on the production floor, build trust with the team, learn the systems, and map the operational back end leadership currently carries.
* By 60 days: Take ownership of the administrative, sourcing, and quality back end, and establish a weekly accountability rhythm that ensures follow-through on leadership initiatives.
* By 90 days: Production tracking and KPIs are live, scrap and quality improvements are underway, and the new production operation launch is on track.
* By 6 to 12 months: Both owners are extracted from day-to-day operations, production lines are running at full multi-shift capacity, and the business is operating as a self-managing machine on track toward its growth targets.

**Company Overview**

Visual Graphic Systems (VGS) is a national manufacturer of architectural signage, environmental graphics, commercial printing, and custom fabrication. We run an established 100,000 sq ft manufacturing operation in New Jersey and are growing in Nashville following our acquisition of ImageLife. We're investing in people, processes, equipment, and capacity to support national growth, and we're looking for the leader to drive that in Nashville.

**Overview**

We are seeking a Director of Manufacturing Operations to lead the growth, performance, and development of our **Nashville facility** . You'll report directly to the CEO, lead through department heads and supervisors, build systems that scale, and help shape our facility, equipment, and workforce investments. This is a strategic leadership role, not a hands-on production position. **This role cannot be performed remotely, and we are not accepting out-of-state remote applicants for this position.** Some travel to our New Jersey facility is needed, especially during onboarding and early growth.

**Responsibilities**

* Lead production planning, scheduling, capacity, quality, safety, and on-time delivery through your department leaders
* Set clear, measurable expectations and hold teams accountable
* Work closely with project management, purchasing, engineering, estimating, and sales
* Build and execute a scalable plan for Nashville manufacturing growth
* Partner with the CEO on facility layout, capital investments, equipment selection, and commissioning
* Learn our New Jersey systems and share best practices across both locations
* Recruit and develop supervisors, managers, and production teams
* Build clear reporting structures, performance standards, training plans, and bench strength
* Implement lean manufacturing, standardized workflows, and continuous improvement
* Track KPIs including on-time delivery, throughput, labor efficiency, first-pass quality, rework, equipment utilization, and cost
* Manage operating budgets, workforce plans, and capital recommendations with a focus on margin and ROI

**What You Bring**

* 10+ years of progressive manufacturing operations experience, including plant or senior operations leadership
* Experience running complex, multi-department operations, ideally $10M to $20M+ in annual production
* Experience leading 50 to 100+ employees through managers and supervisors
* A proven track record with lean manufacturing, scheduling, continuous improvement, metrics, and cost control
* The ability to build teams, scale systems, plan equipment investments, and execute growth
* Willingness to travel to New Jersey as needed

**Nice to Have**

* Experience in architectural signage, commercial printing, large-format graphics, custom fabrication, or related manufacturing
* Custom, project-based, or made-to-order production experience (CNC, digital print, metal fabrication, finishing, assembly)
* Facility expansion, multi-site coordination, or major equipment implementation experience
* A bachelor's degree in engineering, operations, manufacturing, or business, or Lean Six Sigma certification

Signage experience is a plus but not required. Proven manufacturing leadership and the ability to scale matter most.

**Who You Are**

You're direct, decisive, and accountable. You lead through managers, communicate well with executives, and drive change while keeping your people engaged.

**What Success Looks Like**

* **First 90 days:** Learn our New Jersey systems, build relationships at both sites, assess Nashville workflows, staffing, equipment, and capacity, set baseline KPIs, and present an operations roadmap to the CEO.
* **First 6 months:** Tighten scheduling, accountability, and procedures. Build staffing and leadership plans and a phased capacity growth plan.
* **First 12 months:** Show measurable gains in quality, productivity, and delivery, and put systems in place for long-term growth.

**Why VGS**

* Report directly to the CEO with real influence over the company's direction
* Build and shape a growing manufacturing operation
* Back an established national company that's investing in growth.

* Dental insurance
* Flexible spending account
* Health insurance
* Health savings account
* Life insurance
* Paid time off
* Retirement plan
* Vision insurance

Experience:

* progressive manufacturing operations : 10 years (Required)
* leading 50 to 100+ employees : 5 years (Preferred)
* running complex, multi-department operations : 5 years (Preferred)

We require a diverse range of skills to support our work in the markets that drive our business and welcome candidates from all backgrounds and life stages who are passionate about making a difference. **Position Overview: Director of Engineering – Enrichment Operations** As the Director of Engineering for BWXT Enrichment Operations, you will lead the full engineering function responsible for delivering a production‑ready centrifuge product and a high‑precision, highly automated factory capability. • Deliver engineering solutions capable of automotive‑pace production with aerospace‑grade quality.

• Ensure all engineering designs and processes meet nuclear regulatory, DOE, safety, and BWXT quality requirements.  
• Embed compliance gates, audit readiness, and pre‑release checks throughout development. Program Controls & Schedule

• Define technical acceptance criteria for supplier parts, processes, tooling, and special manufacturing steps.  
• Support supplier onboarding speed, delivery performance, and technical readiness to protect schedule-critical components. Cross-Functional Collaboration

• Strong expertise in advanced manufacturing, automation, precision machining, assembly, metrology, and inspection systems.  
• Must be a U.S. citizen capable of obtaining and maintaining a DOE Q clearance; active clearance preferred.

* Overview
  
  At InventWood, we're doing something remarkable. We're bringing SuperWood to life — a revolutionary advanced material that's set to change industries. Our manufacturing plant in Frederick, MD is the beating heart of that mission, and we're looking for an exceptional Plant Manager to lead it.
* Description
  
  Are you a seasoned manufacturing leader who thrives on building something extraordinary from the ground up? Do you want your work to genuinely matter — not just to a bottom line, but to the world? If so, we'd love to meet you.
  
  At InventWood, we're doing something remarkable. We're bringing SuperWood to life — a revolutionary advanced material that's set to change industries. Our manufacturing plant in Frederick, MD is the beating heart of that mission, and we're looking for an exceptional Plant Manager to lead it.
  
  This isn't a role for someone who wants to manage the status quo. This is a rare opportunity to build a team, shape a culture, and lead a plant from its very first day of operation. If you've ever wanted to put your fingerprints on something that lasts, this is it.
  
  What You'll Be Leading
  
  You'll have full responsibility for the safe, efficient, and inspiring operation of our pilot manufacturing plant. That means:
  
  Safety Leadership
  
    + Set and model the gold standard for safety culture — not because regulations require it, but because our people come first. Your behaviour will make it clear, every single day, that safety always comes before production.
    + Identify, establish, and communicate safety procedures that go beyond OSHA compliance to ensure a genuinely injury-free workplace.
    + Serve as the administrator of our Secova/SAMS EHS system, ensuring all training records, safety incidents, and inspections are accurately logged and up to date.
    + Collaborate closely with safety management personnel in our Advanced Materials Innovation Lab to ensure safe, consistent operations across the entire facility.
    + Coordinate emergency response planning with external providers including the fire department, environmental spill containment services, police, and confined space rescue personnel.
  
  Building & Leading Your Team
  
    + Hire our very first production crew — people who genuinely share InventWood's values and principles — and set them up for success from day one.
    + Develop every team member toward a top operator designation, with the capability to safely and confidently operate any machine center on the pilot line.
    + Begin this development during commissioning, ensuring operators and maintenance technicians receive early, structured training with clear expectations for each individual machine.
    + Lead daily operational direction for the pilot line team, keeping production of SuperWood aligned with our quality standards and sales plan.
  
  Commissioning & Startup
  
    + Partner with our engineering team, OEM suppliers, and contractors to bring the pilot line online safely, on schedule, and within budget.
    + Ensure that no trial is run without your full accountability — including planning for expected downtime and delivering clear, useful trial results.
    + Support the selection of a controls technician to maintain and operate the process control network (PCN) and connected PLCs.
  
  Process Control & Continuous Improvement
  
    + Work alongside the Senior Process Engineer to establish robust production reporting, grounded in reliable process control data.
    + Instill a disciplined one-change-at-a-time process control mindset — ensuring parameter changes are deliberate, documented, and fully understood before further adjustments are made.
    + Use data to build a culture of continuous improvement, identifying gaps in safety, downtime, cycle time, and quality as opportunities to improve both performance and profitability.
    + Collaborate with the technical team to plan and execute lab and pilot machine trials that advance the quality and efficiency of SuperWood production.
  
  Environmental & Regulatory Compliance
  
    + Communicate proactively with regulatory officials and work with the technical team to measure all effluent and emissions from the process, validating our environmental modeling.
    + Ensure all pressure vessel equipment is inspected in accordance with applicable operating permits.
    + Maintain open, productive relationships with county and state officials on occupancy permits, environmental construction permits, and economic development programmes.
  
  Budget & Business Management
  
    + Establish and manage an annual operating and maintenance budget, with full accountability to the COO for performance against approved spend.
    + Oversee the inventory rotation of raw materials and finished goods, reporting both to the COO on a regular basis.
    + Follow established PO, invoicing, and receiving processes in partnership with the Accounting team, ensuring parts inventory values are accurately tracked and all assets reported.
    + Provide the Sales team with a monthly production plan, ensure orders are precisely prepared and delivered, and support the swift resolution of any customer claims or complaints.
  
  Supplier & Stakeholder Relationships
  
    + Maintain strong working relationships with wood and chemical suppliers, ensuring material specifications, quality standards, pricing agreements, and safety requirements (including MSDS compliance) are consistently met.
    + Serve as the key point of contact with OEM partners, providing InventWood feedback on equipment operation, maintenance, warranty claims, and delivery.
    + Liaise with the landlord on building structural changes and construction matters in accordance with the lease agreement, including maintenance, snow removal, traffic control, and security.
    + Keep the office manager informed of any site matters affecting office personnel, and actively support a culture of celebration, teamwork, and shared community across the whole facility.
  
  Confidentiality
  
    + Maintain the strictest confidentiality around operating processes, parameters, and targets when engaging with anyone outside of InventWood. What we're building is special — and protecting it matters.
  
  What We're Looking For
  
    + Bachelor's degree (or higher) in Materials Science, Engineering, Business, or a related field
    + 10+ years of manufacturing leadership or supervisory experience
    + 5+ years of experience running a manufacturing plant
    + Experience in an early-stage or high-growth environment — you know how to build, not just maintain
    + Strong grasp of budgeting, lean operations, strategic planning, and working capital management
    + Sharp analytical and problem-solving skills with exceptional attention to detail
    + A confident, clear communicator — with your team, with regulators, and with senior leadership
    + Proficient in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint)

    + Skilled at managing competing priorities, staying organised under pressure, and keeping calm when it counts
  
  Physical Demands
  
  This is a hands-on, plant-floor leadership role and we want to be upfront about what that involves:
  
    + Regular, on-site presence during core business hours is essential — this role cannot be done remotely.
    + You'll need to be available outside of standard hours when project deadlines or operational issues require it. Plant life doesn't always keep office hours, and we appreciate leaders who understand that.
    + You'll be working in an active industrial environment that includes working at heights, in confined spaces, climbing stairs and ladders, and operating in conditions that may include extreme heat or cold. Appropriate safety equipment and procedures will always be in place.
    + You'll regularly move between departments and areas of our facility — from the plant floor to the lab, office spaces, and loading areas.
    + Limited travel may be required from time to time — to visit customers, suppliers, or attend company meetings.
    + Vision and hearing must be within, or correctable to within, normal range.
  
  We are committed to making reasonable accommodations for individuals with disabilities to ensure everyone who is right for this role has a fair opportunity to succeed.
  
  Why InventWood?
  
  Because here, your leadership will shape more than a plant — it will shape a company, a culture, and a product that the world hasn't seen before. You'll work alongside brilliant, passionate people who are as committed to doing things right as they are to doing remarkable things.
  
  We celebrate together, solve hard problems together, and hold ourselves to high standards — together.
  
  Ready to build something that matters?
  
  We can't wait to hear from you.

**VP of Operations – MEP Contractor (DFW)**

**Position summary**

The VP of Operations owns every project from first takeoff to final closeout and is accountable for converting backlog into gross profit at or above the bid margin. This is a senior executive role with full responsibility for estimating, pre-construction, BIM/VDC, project delivery, QAQC, and the operations team.

**About the company.** Staxmatic is a mechanical, plumbing, and HVAC contractor doing commercial ground-up construction across the Dallas–Fort Worth market. We self-perform management, engineering coordination, and supervision, and buy out field labor to qualified trade subcontractors. Projects range from $6M to $300M in MEP contract value, with durations of six months to four years, across sectors such as healthcare, data centers, multifamily, education, hospitality, office, and industrial/distribution. Our team, and most of our general contractor and owner customers, run projects in Procore.

**Why this role is different.** Because field labor is subcontracted, our margin is made in estimating, buyout, coordination, and change management, and contractor performance rather than W2 labor productivity. The VP of Operations must be equally strong at commercial control of subcontractors and at technical command of MEP systems.

**Reporting structure**

Reports to the CEO/Owners. Direct reports: Operations Manager and the leads for Estimating, Preconstruction, BIM/VDC, and QA/QC. Indirect reports: all Project Managers, Assistant Project Managers, Superintendents, and Foremen.

**Key responsibilitiesEstimating, bidding, and costing**

* Set estimating standards: quantity takeoff methods, labor-unit and subcontractor pricing, equipment quotes, escalation and allowances, and scope sheets/bid leveling for every trade package.
* Lead pricing strategy for hard-bid, negotiated, GMP, design-assist, and design-build MEP work.
* Close the loop between estimate and actual: feed job cost history back into pricing and hold a formal estimate-to-budget turnover on every awarded job.

**Preconstruction and design-assist**

* Lead pre-construction services for GCs and owners: conceptual and schematic budgets, value engineering (VE) and target-value design, constructability reviews, and system selection.
* Manage long-lead procurement strategy for major equipment (chillers, AHUs, RTUs, boilers, switchgear interfaces, generators) and escalation risk.
* Review prime contracts and subcontract terms for risk: scope gaps, pay-when-paid, liquidated damages, warranty, indemnity, and design responsibility.

**BIM / VDC and coordination**

* Direct the BIM/VDC group: LOD 300–400 MEP models, clash detection and resolution, coordination meetings, and sign-off of coordinated drawings before fabrication or installation.
* Drive prefabrication and modularization (multi-trade racks, bathroom pods, mechanical skids) through subcontractors and fabrication partners.
* Ensure models flow to field layout (robotic total station), shop drawings, and as-builts.

**Project execution and subcontractor management**

* Accountable for safe, on-time, on-budget delivery of the full portfolio through the Operations Manager, Project Managers, Assistant Project Managers, Superintendents, and Foremen.
* Own the subcontractor model: pre-qualification, buyout, subcontract scope and terms, bonding and insurance compliance, manpower commitments, and performance scorecards.
* Run monthly project reviews (cost-to-complete, work-in-progress/WIP schedule, cash flow, schedule, and risk register) for every active job.
* Oversee submittals, RFIs, three-week look-ahead, commissioning, TAB (testing, adjusting, and balancing), turnover, O&M manuals, and closeout.

**Margin protection and financial control**

* Protect and grow gross profit from bid to closeout; target zero **profit fade** on the portfolio.
* Enforce disciplined change management: timely notice, pricing, and execution of change orders (PCOs/CORs), and no unapproved extra work.
* Manage buyout savings, contingency drawdown, claims, back charges, retainage, and over/under billings with the CFO.
* Approve monthly cost-to-complete forecasts and percent-complete (POC) revenue recognition inputs.

**Quality control / quality assurance**

* Build and own the QA/QC program: preinstallation meetings, first-work inspections, pressure and duct leakage tests, startup checklists, and punch-list management.
* Reduce rework and warranty callbacks; track cost of quality on every job.
* Coordinate with commissioning agents and AHJ inspectors to achieve first-time pass rates.

**Safety**

* Partner with the HSE Manager to champion a zero-incident culture and hold subcontractors to company and GC safety requirements.

**Technology and Procore**

* Own Procore as the operating system of the business: project setup standards, financial tools, change events, RFIs, submittals, inspections/observations, daily logs, and integration with the ERP/accounting system and the estimating platform.
* Use project dashboards and KPIs to manage by exception.
* Enforce the full utilization of Procore by all team members.

**People and leadership**

* Responsible for the continuous development of recruiters, develop and retain Project Managers, APMs, Superintendents, Foremen, estimators, and VDC staff; build succession and a career ladder from APM to Senior PM to Operations Manager.
* Work in tandem with the operations manager
* Serve on the executive team; contribute to strategy, annual budget, backlog planning, and customer relationships with key GCs and owners.

* Track record delivering ground-up commercial projects of $30M+ MEP contract value, with at least one project or program above $100M.
* Hands-on background in both estimating and project management; able to read and challenge an MEP estimate line by line.
* Demonstrated margin results: documented gross profit pickup (gain) versus fade across a multi-year portfolio.
* Experience managing a subcontracted-labor or hybrid model, including subcontract buyout, scope leveling, and subcontractor default management.
* Fluency with contract forms, GMP and lump-sum structures, and change-order law basics.

## Full Job Description

ABOUT THE TEAM

KRUSH Tech is an international technology company developing advanced hardware solutions for defense, aerospace, communications, and autonomous systems. We're launching our U.S. operations from the ground up, building a next-generation, vertically integrated aerospace organization focused on advanced uncrewed aircraft systems (UAS), autonomy, and sensing technologies for the U.S. market and strategic partners. Our teams work across RF, embedded systems, electronics, mechanical engineering, software, manufacturing, and supply chain to turn some of the industry's most demanding engineering challenges into reliable, production-ready solutions, combining the agility of a startup with the ambition to compete at the leading edge of UAS and autonomous systems.

ABOUT THE JOB

We are seeking a Director of Quality to develop and lead the quality strategy for our manufacturing operations, ensuring that our products, processes, and services consistently meet customer, regulatory, and business requirements. This executive leadership role oversees Quality Assurance, Quality Control, Supplier Quality, and Continuous Improvement, driving a culture of quality excellence, compliance, risk management, and operational performance.

Reporting to the Vice President of the site, you will build the quality organization and management system as KRUSH launches U.S. manufacturing. This is a rare opportunity to define how quality is run in a new U.S. aerospace and defense manufacturing operation from day one.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

* Develop and execute the quality vision, strategy, and objectives, aligned with business goals and customer expectations
* Provide leadership and direction to quality teams at our Austin site and, as KRUSH grows, across additional sites
* Build and maintain a culture focused on quality, compliance, and continuous improvement, and serve as executive sponsor for quality programs across the organization
* Oversee the design, implementation, and continuous improvement of the Quality Management System (QMS), ensuring compliance with ISO 9001, AS9100, and other applicable industry-specific requirements
* Establish quality policies, procedures, and governance frameworks, and monitor QMS effectiveness through audits, performance metrics, and management reviews
* Lead customer quality initiatives, including rapid resolution of quality issues, customer complaint processes, and corrective action programs, to improve customer satisfaction and product reliability, in partnership with Operations, Engineering, and Commercial teams

* Establish supplier quality standards and performance requirements, and lead supplier qualification, development, and audit programs
* Drive supplier performance improvements and risk mitigation, partnering with Procurement and Supply Chain to ensure quality throughout the supply network
* Champion Lean, Six Sigma, and continuous improvement methodologies, and lead root cause analysis and problem-solving initiatives
* Drive reductions in defects, waste, scrap, rework, and Cost of Poor Quality (COPQ), and establish quality improvement roadmaps with measurable performance goals
* Ensure compliance with regulatory, customer, and industry requirements, oversee internal, customer, regulatory, and certification audits, and lead risk management for product quality and compliance, including product safety and reliability programs
* Build, lead, mentor, and develop the quality team as the organization grows, including succession planning and talent development programs
* Build organizational capability in quality methodologies and best practices, and promote teamwork, accountability, and continuous learning
* Develop and manage quality department budgets, and monitor and improve Cost of Quality (COQ) and COPQ
* Support strategic business planning and growth initiatives, and provide executive-level reporting on quality performance, risks, and improvement opportunities
* Establish and track quality KPIs, including customer complaint rate, customer satisfaction, COPQ, First Pass Yield, defect and non-conformance rates, supplier quality performance, audit finding closure, scrap and rework reduction, CAPA effectiveness, and quality system compliance

**  
Requirements**  
* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Quality Management, Manufacturing, Science, or a related field
* 10+ years of progressive quality leadership experience
* 5+ years of senior management or director-level experience
* Extensive experience with Quality Management Systems (ISO 9001, AS9100, or equivalent) and regulatory compliance
* Experience leading Quality Assurance, Quality Control, Supplier Quality, and continuous improvement functions
* Strong skills in audit management, supplier and customer quality management, risk management, root cause analysis and problem solving, data analytics and KPI management, and financial and budget management
* Experience with Lean manufacturing and Six Sigma
* Strong strategic thinking, executive leadership, change management, and stakeholder management skills
* Must qualify as a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export-controlled information or facilities (ITAR)

  
**Benefits**

KRUSH Tech offers a competitive compensation package. Compensation is determined by role, level, location, and alignment with market data. Individual offers are determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on interview performance, job-related skills, relevant education and experience, certifications, and internal equity.

The salary range provided is a good faith estimate of the applicable range as of the date of posting. The final offer will be determined after considering all relevant factors, including a candidate's qualifications and experience.

In addition to base pay, KRUSH Tech offers a monthly benefits stipend that employees can apply toward the health, dental, vision, or other coverage that best fits their needs, along with 9 paid federal holidays per year.

**Equal Opportunity Employer**

KRUSH Tech is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to fostering an inclusive workplace and providing equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, protected veteran status, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

**Reasonable Accommodation Statement**

KRUSH Tech is committed to providing reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities throughout the application and hiring process and during employment. If you require assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, please contact Human Resources.
